make.name: Kia
make.description: South Korean carmaker founded in 1944 and part of Hyundai Motor Group, with Hyundai Motor Company its largest shareholder. Its dedicated EVs (EV2 to EV9) use the E-GMP platform family; the EV6 was 2022 European Car of the Year, the EV9 2024 World Car of the Year and the EV3 2025 World Car of the Year.

models.name: EV6
models.description: Kia's first dedicated electric car (2021), a low crossover on the 800 V E-GMP platform shared with the Hyundai Ioniq 5. It was 2022 European Car of the Year; a facelift with bigger batteries followed in 2024.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Kia's first dedicated EV on the 800 V E-GMP platform, with 58 kWh and 77.4 kWh packs; the 576 hp EV6 GT arrived in late 2022.

generations.name: Facelift
generations.description: Revealed May 2024: new lights and cabin, packs grow to 63 kWh and 84 kWh; US cars (MY2025 on) are built in Georgia with a NACS port. The GT is not in the US 2026 or 2027 price lists.

models.name: EV9
models.description: Kia's three-row electric SUV, on sale since 2023 and built in Korea and Georgia (USA). It won 2024 World Car of the Year.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Three-row E-GMP SUV launched in 2023 (US model year 2024), built in Korea and since May 2024 in West Point, Georgia. The 501 hp EV9 GT went on sale in Europe in 2025; its US launch was put on hold in November 2025.

models.name: EV3
models.description: Kia's compact electric crossover, launched in 2024 and 2025 World Car of the Year. It reached the US in 2026 as a 2027 model and is Kia's cheapest US EV.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Compact crossover on the 400 V version of E-GMP, launched in Korea in July 2024 and Europe in late 2024; AWD and GT versions from 2026, and US sales from model year 2027 (built in Mexico, NACS port).

models.name: EV4
models.description: Kia's first dedicated electric car that is not an SUV, sold as a sedan and, in Europe, a hatchback since 2025. A US launch planned for early 2026 was postponed indefinitely in October 2025.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Sedan (built in Gwangmyeong, Korea) and Europe-only hatchback (built in Zilina, Slovakia) on the 400 V E-GMP; AWD and GT versions added in 2026.

models.name: EV5
models.description: Two-row mid-size electric SUV launched in China in 2023, then built in Korea from 2025 for Korea, Europe and Canada. Kia has said it will not be sold in the United States.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Mid-size two-row SUV. China-built cars (from 2023) use BYD FinDreams LFP packs on the N3 eK platform; Korea-built cars (from 2025, Europe and Korea) use CATL NMC packs on the 400 V E-GMP.

variants.name: Standard Range FWD (64.2 kWh LFP, China-built)
Long Range FWD (88.1 kWh LFP, China-built)
Long Range AWD (88.1 kWh LFP, China-built)
Standard Range FWD (60.3 kWh NMC, Korea-built)
Long Range FWD (81.4 kWh NMC, Korea-built)
Long Range AWD (81.4 kWh NMC, Korea-built)

models.name: EV2
models.description: Kia's smallest dedicated EV, a boxy supermini sold in Europe since 2026 as the successor to the e-Soul.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Supermini on the 400 V E-GMP, unveiled January 2026 and built in Zilina, Slovakia, from March 2026 for Europe.

models.name: Niro EV
models.description: Battery-electric version of Kia's Niro crossover (e-Niro in Europe), sold from 2018 over two generations. Kia discontinued it in 2026; the facelifted Niro is hybrid-only.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Battery-electric version of the first Niro (e-Niro in Europe), sharing its powertrain with the Hyundai Kona Electric; 64 kWh and, outside the US, 39.2 kWh packs.

generations.name: Second generation
generations.description: Redesigned Niro (SG2) with a 64.8 kWh pack and heat pump; Kia ended the Niro EV in 2026 when the facelifted Niro became hybrid-only.

models.name: Soul EV
models.description: Electric version of the boxy Soul, sold from 2014 to 2024 (e-Soul in Europe). The second generation never reached US showrooms; the EV3 and, in Europe, the EV2 replace it.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Electric version of the second-generation Soul with CHAdeMO fast charging; the 2018 model year raised usable capacity from 27 to 30 kWh.

generations.name: Second generation (e-Soul)
generations.description: Third-generation Soul body with the Niro/Kona Electric powertrain (39.2 or 64 kWh, CCS). Sold in Europe, Korea and Canada; the US launch was cancelled.

models.name: Ray EV
models.description: Electric version of the Ray, a tall Korean-market city car. Kia's first production EV (2011-2018), it returned in 2023 with an LFP battery.

generations.name: Original
generations.description: Kia's first production EV: a Korea-only electric Ray city car with a 16.4 kWh pack, first sold to government fleets.

generations.name: Ray EV (2023)
generations.description: Revived in September 2023 on the facelifted Ray with a 35.2 kWh LFP pack and a much lower price; offered as a 4-seat car and 1- or 2-seat vans.

models.name: PV5
models.description: Mid-size electric van and people carrier, the first of Kia's PV (platform beyond vehicle) range, on sale in Korea and Europe since 2025.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Kia's first dedicated electric van on the E-GMP.S platform, in Passenger, Cargo, chassis-cab and wheelchair-accessible versions.

models.name: PV7
models.description: Full-size electric van above the PV5, unveiled in September 2026 with passenger, cargo and chassis-cab versions.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Full-size 800 V van on E-GMP.S, shown at IAA Transportation in September 2026; Korean and European sales start first.

models.name: Carens Clavis EV
models.description: Three-row electric MPV built and sold in India since July 2025.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Electric version of the facelifted Carens Clavis MPV, Kia's first EV made in India, with 42 or 51.4 kWh packs.

models.name: Syros EV
models.description: Compact electric crossover for India, launched on 22 July 2026.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Electric version of the boxy Syros crossover on the K1 BEV platform, launched in India in July 2026.

models.name: Bongo III EV
models.description: Battery-electric version of Kia's Bongo cab-over light truck for the Korean market.

generations.name: Bongo III EV
generations.description: Electric version of the fourth-generation Bongo light truck, sold in Korea since January 2020.

models.name: KX3 EV
models.description: Electric version of the KX3 small crossover, sold only in China from 2018 by the Dongfeng Yueda Kia joint venture.

generations.name: KX3 EV
generations.description: China-only electric version of the first-generation KX3 crossover, built by Dongfeng Yueda Kia.

legacy_notes.note: EV9 GT-Line AWD: legacy price $54,900 is the Light Standard Range price and 304 mi is the Long Range RWD EPA figure. GT-Line EPA is 270 mi (MY2024-25) / 280 mi (MY2026-27); 2027 GT-Line MSRP $71,990. Mapped to Long Range AWD (GT-Line is a trim, same powertrain).
EV6 GT AWD (2024): pre-facelift GT; specs roughly right (EPA 218 mi MY2024). Marked previous_generation correctly.
Niro 'Wave (2024)': row carries EV6 GT data (77.4 kWh, 576 hp, AWD, 218 mi, 161 mph). The Niro EV is FWD, 64.8 kWh, 201 hp, 253 mi EPA. Duplicate of 208; mapped to second-generation 64.8 kWh.
Niro Wind: same copied EV6 GT specs (576 hp, 218 mi). Wind and Wave are trims of one powertrain; mapped to second-generation 64.8 kWh. The Niro EV is discontinued (2026 was the last US model year).
Niro Wave: range 253 mi is right but battery 77.4 kWh, 576 hp, AWD and 104 mph are wrong; 2026 MSRP is $44,700 (Wave) / $39,700 (Wind). Model is discontinued, not 'available'.

EV6 GT AWD '2025 Facelift': price $44,395 and range 319 mi are wrong (319 mi is the Long Range RWD). The facelift GT was $63,800 (MY2025) with 231 mi EPA, 84 kWh, up to 641 hp; the GT is not in the US 2026/2027 price lists.
EV9 Light RWD = Standard Range RWD (76.1 kWh, 230 mi). OK.
EV9 Light Long Range RWD: legacy 0-60 9.4 s is the official 0-100 km/h figure; mapped to Long Range RWD.
EV9 Wind AWD: trim of Long Range AWD; merged.
EV9 Land AWD: trim of Long Range AWD; merged.
EV6 Light RWD (pre-facelift 58 kWh Standard Range).
EV6 Light Long Range RWD: trim of pre-facelift Long Range RWD; merged with 73 and 75.
EV6 Wind RWD: trim of pre-facelift Long Range RWD; merged.
EV6 GT-Line RWD: trim of pre-facelift Long Range RWD; merged.
EV6 Light Long Range AWD: trim of pre-facelift Long Range AWD; merged with 74 and 76.
EV6 Wind AWD: trim of pre-facelift Long Range AWD; merged.
EV6 GT-Line AWD: 252 mi is the 20-inch-wheel EPA figure of the pre-facelift Long Range AWD; merged.

gaps: No sourced US MSRPs for pre-facelift EV6 (MY2022-2024), MY2024 EV9, first-generation Niro EV or MY2018 Soul EV; legacy prices for these rows look like real MY2024 figures but could not be verified (web search quota ran out).
EV9 US charge port (CCS1 vs NACS by model year) not sourced; connector left null. Niro EV US connector for second generation also left null.
EV9 GT: EPA-certified (260 mi, MY2026) but US launch postponed indefinitely in Nov 2025; no US offering recorded. EV9 GT 501 hp is the Kia US estimate (374 kW in Europe).
EV4 GT and EV4 sedan AWD exist per Wikipedia but only hatchback AWD/GT data was found.
EV5 China-built AWD (88.1 kWh LFP): no sourced market price/range; China CLTC AWD figure reported as 630 km (Gasgoo) vs 650 km (electrive).
EV5 60.3 kWh EU price is the Netherlands price (Germany not listed).
European prices are German list prices from EV Database (not maker price lists); WLTP ranges also from EV Database.
Horsepower, torque and top speed for non-US variants are unit conversions of the kW/Nm/km/h figures in the cited sources.
Bongo III EV battery size and Ray EV DC charging power not sourced. Ray EV 2023 range is the Korean certified figure from Kia Korea.
PV7: production timing (late 2026) and specs come only from Wikipedia; Standard Range power and any range figure not sourced.
PV5 Cargo variants (43.3 kWh LFP Europe, 51.5 kWh) only partly modelled; Passenger 7-seat versions not split out.
KX3 EV battery, range and exact end date not sourced (Wikipedia's source link is dead); end_year 2019 is the end of the KX3 first generation.
No verified photos for Ray EV (2023), Carens Clavis EV, Syros EV or Bongo III EV (Commons files found showed the combustion versions).
Syros EV Extended Range price is the cheapest 'ER' variant (Rs 17.00 lakh); Autocar India does not map packs to every trim.
